newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt faces opposition on energy reform.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt faces opposition on energy reform.

text.p: Opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said on Tuesday they oppose Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt's plans to encourage competition in the energy sector.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet has been dragging its heels on reform legislation it initially hoped to discuss in July. Rexrodt later said the cabinet would take up reform legislation this month, but a spokeswoman for his ministry said it would likely be delayed until October.

Rexrodt aims to end regional monopolies in Germany's electricity and gas markets in 1997 and prepare for cross-border competition with utilities in neighbouring countries, in line with an agreement reached by European energy ministers in June.
Volker Jung, energy spokesman for the SPD parliamentary faction, said the planned bill would not lead to fair competition or environmentally friendly energy supply.
Nor does the bill pay sufficient heed to the rights of local communities to govern energy supply, Jung said.
"Rexrodt's proposals would not lead to more competition, but to a greater concentration in the utilities sector that would threaten the existence of many municipal works," Jung said.
